clue.text: Before entering parliament with backing, see what people are saying

indicators.note: entering signals that the word for before goes inside the parliament word
with backing means the parliament's name is read from back to front

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
pre is the Latin-derived prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone about to take a seat in parliament, with supporters behind them, gauges public opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish parliament's name, read backwards, is cut open by the prefix for before; 'see' is the definition's verb, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading means following speech by watching mouth movements, so it lets you see words spoken.

clue.text: Plenty, especially after 18 (see posters)

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
posters are advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: A note directing the reader to some posters for a plentiful supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET: 'bucketloads' is the idiom the definition points at.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is informal for a great quantity, heard especially in bucketloads.

clue.text: Awfully hot in cold place causing problem, in a way

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for a cold place

parts.note: a pole, north or south, is a famously cold place

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of hot are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Terrible heat in a frozen region causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' here means a road, so the problem is one in a road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface, a problem on the way.

clue.text: Make money from loch

definitions.meaning: Loch ... is a lake in Perthshire, Scotland

explanation.surface: Getting an income out of a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning is gaining money by labour; Earn is also the name of a Scottish loch.

clue.text: Double-crossing as a game?

parts.note: a duplicate is a double, an exact copy
a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: Is betraying someone just a sport?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-crossing' reads as treachery but splits into double and crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicate bridge is a form of the card game in which the same deals are replayed by other players.

clue.text: Substitute what's on one's mind at station?

parts.note: a stop is a station on a route
London Underground warns passengers to 'mind the gap' at the platform edge

explanation.surface: Something to stand in for what you worry about while waiting at a station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube announcement 'Mind the gap' makes the gap what you mind at a station.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary replacement used until something better is found.

clue.text: State aid, so majority in parliament speculate about fine mess

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus or so

indicators.note: majority in means most of the word, with its final letters cut off

parts.note: the Knesset is Israel's parliament

indicators.note: about means the word for speculate goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: to bet is to speculate, gamble

indicators.note: mess signals the letters of fine are muddled

explanation.surface: So the ruling side in parliament gambles on a fine muddle over state handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority in' drops the last two letters of Israel's parliament; 'about' puts the gamble round the muddled letters of fine, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness benefit was a UK state payment to people too ill to work.

clue.text: No breach? Not quite, with half 7s in bother

definitions.text: No breach? Not quite, with half 7s in bother

indicators.note: in bother signals the letters are in a state of disorder, to be rearranged
not quite means the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: the phrase is used as written

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters

parts.note: the number seven written out, plural

explanation.surface: Is there no breach at all, given a little rugby sevens trouble?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts NO BREACH to NOBREAC; 'half' takes SEV from SEVENS; 'in bother' shuffles the ten letters. Observance is itself no breach of a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Observance is keeping a rule or custom, the opposite of breaking it.

clue.text: About a thousand pounds for article on Spanish city

indicators.note: about means the thousand-pound word goes round the single letter

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Roughly a thousand pounds paid for an item about a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts A inside GRAND to make GRANAD, and the article A goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Stones with a change of note in Scotland

indicators.note: change of note means one musical note letter is swapped for another

parts.note: pebbles are small stones

explanation.surface: Rocks rearranged into a different tune north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The note B is replaced by the note E.
explanation.definitionFit: Peebles is a town in the Scottish Borders, so it lies in Scotland.

clue.text: Human error in pact with rhino

indicators.note: error in suggests a mistake that scrambles the letters

explanation.surface: A person blunders while making an agreement with a rhinoceros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human error' reads as one phrase, but 'Human' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropic means relating to human beings, from Greek anthropos, man.

clue.text: Object of calling with 18

definitions.meaning: to call a ... a ... is to speak plainly
a bucket and ... are the child's seaside pair

explanation.surface: The thing summoned along with a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The spade is what is called by its name in the plain-speaking idiom, and goes with a bucket at the beach.

clue.text: See 18
Food supply, last in hand for neighbour to bull with 18

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word hand

parts.note: on a dartboard the inner ring lies next to the bull
a pail is a bucket, the answer at 18

explanation.surface: A farmer feeds the animal next to the bull from a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET, whose synonym PAIL ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner pail is a container carrying a worker's meal.

clue.text: Visual, without particular taste, like type of polygon

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the eye word surrounds the taste word

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eyes, visual
a tang is a sharp distinctive flavour

explanation.surface: Something seen but lacking any distinctive flavour, shaped like a geometric figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Octangular describes a shape with eight angles, as in an octagon.

clue.text: English region's acknowledgement to French

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: merci is French for thank you
a is French for to

explanation.surface: A region of England thanks France.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the Midlands of England.

clue.text: Lord Coe entertaining a fool to fish

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside, so the name surrounds the letter

parts.note: Seb Coe, Lord Coe, is a British Olympic runner and administrator
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: The peer and athlete hosts a clown on a fishing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe is the British middle-distance runner who led the London 2012 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bass is a food fish of coastal waters.

clue.text: Go right through quietly before holding nurse at war

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: holding means the before word contains the nurse

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a VAD was a Voluntary Aid Detachment nurse in the world wars

explanation.surface: A nurse in wartime moves silently ahead to get completely through.
explanation.walkthrough: VAD nurses served with British forces in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervade is to spread throughout something.

clue.text: Orders Scotch for two right at the end of the 1940s

parts.note: POs are postal orders
twa is the Scots word for two

explanation.surface: Ordering a whisky for a couple of people right as the decade closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but means Scots dialect here. Postal orders are UK money orders bought at post offices.
explanation.definitionFit: The late 1940s came just after the Second World War, so they were the period after the war.

clue.text: Tester takes time to enter payment

indicators.note: to enter means the time word goes into the payment word

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An examiner sets aside a period before handing over a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in chemistry to detect or test for another.

clue.text: Dollar for aliens' dance from shady business

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar
ETs are extraterrestrials, aliens
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Paying a dollar to see extraterrestrials dance in some dodgy enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aliens'' gives ETS, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket shop is a dubious firm, such as an unlicensed broker or cut-price travel agent.

clue.text: High spot for woman and others

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A lofty place for one lady and everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, the highest spot on Earth.

clue.text: Stupendous animal, horse reportedly, going round Ireland

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: going round means the horse letters surround the word for Ireland
reportedly means the word is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, sounding like the letters G G
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An astonishing creature, a horse they say, circling round Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee, nursery talk for a horse, is spoken as two letters, and they sit either side of the poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering means astounding, so overwhelming as to make you reel.

clue.text: Constituency maybe following 18 in transport

definitions.meaning: a bucket ... is a contoured car ...

explanation.surface: An electoral district coming after a bucket on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET, giving bucket seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP holds a seat, meaning a constituency; a bucket seat is a single shaped car seat.

clue.text: God of old said to increase tension

indicators.note: said means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: to tighten is to make something more taut

explanation.surface: An ancient deity is said to wind up the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Titans were the Greek gods before the Olympians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the elder gods of Greek myth, overthrown by Zeus.

clue.text: Excitement to be fatal with 18

definitions.meaning: to ... the bucket is to die

explanation.surface: A thrill that turns deadly alongside a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick is a buzz of pleasure; kicking the bucket is the idiom for dying.

clue.text: Revolutionary invention to raise water after 18

definitions.meaning: something that turns round, an epoch-making invention
a bucket ... lifts water in buckets fixed round its rim

explanation.surface: A ground-breaking device for lifting water that comes after a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BUCKET; 'Revolutionary' puns on turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheel revolves and was a landmark invention; a bucket wheel scoops water upwards.

clue.text: Shy old copper, if well outside sanctum

parts.note: d was the old British penny, a copper coin

indicators.note: outside means the healthy word surrounds the private room

parts.note: fit means healthy, well
a den is a private retreat, a sanctum

explanation.surface: A timid retired policeman, if in good health, stays out of his study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is a coin: d, the old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffident means lacking self-confidence, timid.

clue.text: I've left off working on Hebridean island

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A worker on a Scottish island gives up their job.
explanation.walkthrough: TIREE is one of the Inner Hebrides, islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person can say they've stopped their working life.

clue.text: Have a break from backing undiluted a rebel within

indicators.note: within means the rebel's name goes inside the reversed word
backing means the word for undiluted is read in reverse

parts.note: neat means without water, undiluted
Robert Ket led the Norfolk rebellion of 1549

explanation.surface: Taking a pause from supporting a straight rebel inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebel's name sits inside the reversed word for undiluted, after its second letter; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To take ten is the idiom for a short rest of ten minutes.
